title: A Cipher for the Ghost
premise: Bram Delacroix, a nonbinary private security contractor haunted by a botched extraction that killed their team, lives off-grid guarding paranoid clients in a Baltic port city. When an anonymous voiceprint—Bram's own, aged and altered—unlocks a black-site server in Singapore, Bram learns the 'incident' was engineered by their former employer, Halcyon Group, to bury evidence of trafficking routes. Hunted by both Halcyon's cleaners and the ghost of the colleague they thought dead, Bram must decide whether to trade the server's decryption key—the one secret worth killing for—to a journalist before the border checkpoint shift change seals them inside. In the end, Bram chooses truth over loyalty, exposes Halcyon, and finds an unlikely found family among the people they once guarded, finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Beatrix Kavanagh is a former maritime security analyst who spent six years writing risk assessments for clients she can no longer name. She writes thrillers from a rented cottage on the Welsh coast, where the fog does most of her editing.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unlocked Doors
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Establishes Bram's sleepless routine guarding reclusive tech executive Ilse Varga in a Baltic port city; a routine perimeter check reveals someone photographed the safehouse. Emotional beat: hypervigilance as a way of life, and the first crack of dread.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A dead-drop drive contains audio of Bram's own voice—older, rougher—unlocking a Singaporean server. The file metadata points to Halcyon Group, Bram's old employer. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past speaking in your own throat.

chapters.title: Ilse Knows More Than She Says
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse admits she hired Bram not for protection but because Bram's name appeared in leaked Halcyon files. She gives Bram a burner phone and a warning: the cleaners are already en route. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: The Incident, Retold
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, intercut with fragmented memory. Flashback to the failed extraction in Moldova: three teammates dead, one—Mara Reyes—listed as killed in action. Bram replays the night, noticing details that don't fit the official account. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Dawn
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Fleeing the safehouse before it burns, Bram crosses paths with a Halcyon cleaner posing as border police and barely talks their way through. They realize the checkpoint shifts are being manipulated to trap them. Emotional beat: the world narrowing to corridors and timetables.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Waits
chapters.summary: Tomas Lindqvist's POV. Introduce the investigative journalist in Riga holding half a story on Halcyon's trafficking routes, waiting for a source brave enough to hand over the decryption key. Emotional beat: patience as a form of courage.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the voiceprint trail to a decommissioned signal station, Bram finds proof Mara is alive—and working for Halcyon. Emotional beat: hope and betrayal arriving in the same envelope.

chapters.title: What Mara Chose
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara explains why she faked her death: she discovered the routes, was given a choice between complicity and a coffin, and chose to fight from inside. She asks Bram to walk away. Emotional beat: love surviving under a false flag.

chapters.title: The Key
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram realizes the voiceprint wasn't a message—it was a test. Halcyon has been measuring whether Bram could be turned or broken. The decryption key is embedded in Bram's own biometric history. Emotional beat: the horror of being the secret.

chapters.title: Safe House No Longer
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse's estate is raided; she escapes with Bram using escape routes she built for exactly this day. Her calm competence reveals her own buried past with Halcyon. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Halcyon's handler, Director Anselm Roth, offers Bram full reinstatement, a clean record, and Mara's safety—in exchange for delivering the key and silencing Lindqvist. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar uniform.

chapters.title: Night Train to Riga
chapters.summary: Bram and Ilse's POV alternating. On the train, Bram confesses the incident's true failure—their hesitation cost seconds and lives—and Ilse answers with her own confession. Emotional beat: vulnerability as the first act of belonging.

chapters.title: The Dead Drop Burns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Ordered to eliminate Bram, Mara sabotages the operation instead, tipping off the cleaners' positions—but her cover is now blown. Emotional beat: choosing a side out loud, at last.

chapters.title: Rendezvous at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A tense meeting with Lindqvist goes wrong when a cleaner tails them; Ilse draws fire so Bram and the journalist can slip away. Ilse is captured. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Careful Woman
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, in captivity. Roth tries to break Ilse; she stalls, feeds him disinformation, and buys Bram twelve hours. Emotional beat: dignity as resistance.

chapters.title: Everything Bram Carried
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. With Lindqvist, Bram decrypts partial files: names, routes, and confirmation that Roth personally ordered the Moldova ambush. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Offer Refused
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Roth calls directly, holding Ilse as leverage, and demands the key by dawn checkpoint shift change. Bram negotiates a trade: Ilse for the key, knowing they intend to cheat. Emotional beat: cold clarity after years of fog.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the border checkpoint, the trade collapses into chaos: Mara turns her weapon on Halcyon's team, Ilse frees herself, and Bram uploads the key to Lindqvist mid-firefight. Emotional beat: the climax—loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: What the Light Shows
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Roth is arrested through Lindqvist's published files and international pressure; the trafficking routes close. But Mara, wounded, slips away rather than face arrest for her years inside. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The One Who Walked Away
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara leaves a final message for Bram—not forgiveness, but gratitude—and disappears toward a new name and a quieter war. Emotional beat: letting go without erasing.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Weeks later, Bram takes a modest contract protecting a community legal clinic—clients nobody trusts, for reasons worth trusting. Ilse visits; Lindqvist sends clippings. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, quiet and final. Bram sleeps eight hours undisturbed for the first time since Moldova, wakes to ordinary morning light, and lets the alarm ring unanswered. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
